title: Magento to Shopify migration
summary: Preserve products, transactions, search and measurement through a tested cutover.
why: URLs, search traffic and transaction records are assets; omissions interrupt revenue and operations.
Rehearsal and incremental sync expose risks while recovery remains manageable.
know: Inventory URLs, traffic pages, products/variants, customers, orders, media, discounts and integrations.
Permanently redirect each old URL to its closest relevant page; return 404/410 when no replacement exists. For headless, test at the actual receiving route.
Do not assume passwords or logins transfer. Verify historical orders, gift cards and notification side effects separately.
inputs: Old and target URLs, exports, traffic and URL inventory
Included/excluded data, SKU/ID maps and system write ownership
Cutover window, incremental data, decision owner and recovery conditions
actions: Create data mappings, URL/redirect lists, functional gaps and integration inventory.
Dry-run in a test environment. Reconcile SKUs, currencies, counts, relationships and media; isolate notification and tracking side effects.
Plan freezes/incremental sync, DNS, GSC, event deduplication and cutover.
Execute within authorization. Record last sync, cutover checks and recovery boundaries; monitor afterward.
done: High-value old URLs reach relevant indexable pages in one hop, without loops or chains.
Product/order samples, shopping paths, analytics/ad events and consent have test evidence.
Recovery after new orders includes reconciliation, not just a DNS reversal.
pitfalls: Changing positioning, URLs and platform together without a baseline.
Moving products while forgetting GSC, tracking, support or account activation.
decision: Agree on data scope, acceptable downtime and recovery triggers.

reader.concept: Migration moves products, content, customer relationships and search entry points to a new system while preserving the jobs users need to do.
reader.when: Use this for Magento-to-Shopify or platform/URL-structure changes.

example.situation: An old search result points to a product page missing from the new store.
example.lesson: Map and redirect the old URL to the relevant replacement.

reader.first_step: Inventory the data and old URLs with the most traffic or revenue value.

diagram.title: Preserve an old search entry point
diagram.caption: Use a relevant replacement. Without one, return 404/410 as appropriate instead of redirecting everything home.
